metadata.title: Galaxium Travels — ASVS Level 1 Plan of Action and Milestones
metadata.remarks: Generated from audit-findings.md. Scope: Python/FastAPI backend, Java Spring Boot hold service. Controls audited: V4 (Access Control), V5 (Input Validation), V13 (API Security), V14 (HTTP Headers/CORS).

poam-items.title: IDOR on GET /bookings/{user_id} — unauthenticated caller can enumerate any user's bookings
poam-items.description: ASVS V4.1.3: GET /bookings/{user_id} returns all bookings for any caller-supplied user ID without verifying that the authenticated principal owns that user_id, enabling horizontal privilege escalation.

subject-reference.title: V4.1.3 — Users can only access their own resources

remediation-tasks.title: Add ownership check to GET /bookings/{user_id}
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py, lines 169–172. The handler currently calls the service and returns the result with no identity check. Add a JWT bearer dependency (e.g. `Depends(verify_token)`) that extracts the caller's subject claim and compare it to the path parameter `user_id`. If they do not match, raise `HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='Forbidden')` before the DB query is executed. The `verify_token` function should decode and validate the JWT using `python-jose` or `authlib`, reading the secret/public key from an environment variable.

poam-items.title: No authentication middleware — entire FastAPI application is unauthenticated
poam-items.description: ASVS V4.1.5: No authentication dependency, middleware, or decorator exists anywhere in server.py; every endpoint is reachable by unauthenticated requests, violating the deny-by-default principle.

subject-reference.title: V4.1.5 — Access control denies by default

remediation-tasks.title: Introduce global authentication dependency in FastAPI
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py, lines 44–337. Create a new file `booking_system_backend/auth.py` containing an async function `verify_token(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme))` that validates an OAuth 2 JWT bearer token (decode with `python-jose`, verify signature against a public key or shared secret stored in the `JWT_SECRET` environment variable, and raise `HTTPException(401)` on failure). In server.py, import `verify_token` and attach it as a default router dependency: either pass `dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)]` to every `APIRouter`, or add it as `app.dependency_overrides` so all routes inherit it. The `/health` and `/register` endpoints may be explicitly exempted by passing `dependencies=[]` at the route level.

poam-items.title: IDOR on POST /cancel/{booking_id} — any caller can cancel another user's booking
poam-items.description: ASVS V4.2.1: cancel_booking() fetches the booking and cancels it without comparing the booking's user_id against the authenticated caller's identity, enabling any authenticated user to cancel bookings they do not own by iterating IDs.

subject-reference.title: V4.2.1 — IDOR protection on sensitive resources

remediation-tasks.title: Add ownership assertion to POST /cancel/{booking_id}
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 175–186 and booking_system_backend/services/booking.py lines 93–123. In server.py, inject the authenticated caller's user_id from the JWT subject (via `Depends(verify_token)`). Pass `caller_id` as an additional argument to `cancel_booking()`. In services/booking.py, after the DB fetch of the booking (currently line ~97), add: `if booking.user_id != caller_id: return ErrorResponse(error='Forbidden', status_code=403)`. In server.py's cancel handler, check `isinstance(result, ErrorResponse)` and raise `HTTPException(status_code=result.status_code, detail=result.error)` if true.

poam-items.title: POST /internal/bookings/from-hold is publicly reachable — unauthenticated booking forgery
poam-items.description: ASVS V4.2.1: The internal endpoint that converts holds into real bookings is internet-facing and carries no authentication, allowing any attacker to forge arbitrary bookings by calling it directly.

subject-reference.title: V4.2.1 — IDOR protection on sensitive resources

remediation-tasks.title: Protect POST /internal/bookings/from-hold with a shared-secret header
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 221–237. Add a dependency function `verify_internal_secret(x_internal_token: str = Header(...))` that reads a shared secret from the `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` environment variable and raises `HTTPException(403)` if the header value does not match. Apply this dependency to the `/internal/bookings/from-hold` route handler. In the Java service, file booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/client/PythonBackendClient.java, add the same header value (read from the `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` environment variable) to every outbound request to `/internal/bookings/from-hold`. The secret must be at least 32 bytes of cryptographically random data, set via a Docker/ECS secret at deploy time.

poam-items.title: Java HoldController has no authentication — hold operations accessible to any caller
poam-items.description: ASVS V4.2.1: POST /quotes/{quoteId}/holds, POST /holds/{holdId}/confirm, and POST /holds/{holdId}/release carry no Spring Security annotations or filter; any caller who knows or guesses a UUID can confirm or release another user's hold.

subject-reference.title: V4.2.1 — IDOR protection on sensitive resources

remediation-tasks.title: Add Spring Security and @PreAuthorize to HoldController
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/api/HoldController.java lines 19–70. Add `spring-boot-starter-security` and `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server` to pom.xml. Create a `SecurityConfig.java` in the `com.galaxium.holdservice` package that configures `HttpSecurity` to require a valid JWT bearer token for all hold and confirm endpoints, using `.oauth2ResourceServer(oauth2 -> oauth2.jwt(...))`. Annotate the `confirmHold` and `releaseHold` methods with `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")`. In `HoldService`, retrieve the caller's subject from `SecurityContextHolder` and compare it against the `userId` stored on the `Hold` entity, throwing `AccessDeniedException` on mismatch.

poam-items.title: BookingRequest.name has no max_length — oversized payloads accepted
poam-items.description: ASVS V5.1.1: BookingRequest.name is a plain str with no max_length constraint, allowing arbitrarily long strings that can cause excessive memory use or denial-of-service via oversized payloads.

subject-reference.title: V5.1.1 — All string inputs have defined maximum length constraints

remediation-tasks.title: Add max_length=200 to BookingRequest.name in schemas.py
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/schemas.py lines 52–53. Ensure `from pydantic import BaseModel, Field` is imported (add `Field` if not already present). Change the field declaration from `name: str` to `name: str = Field(..., max_length=200)`. No other changes are required; Pydantic will automatically return HTTP 422 with a descriptive error when a request exceeds the limit.

poam-items.title: UserRegistration.name and .email have no max_length — oversized registration payloads accepted
poam-items.description: ASVS V5.1.1: UserRegistration.name and UserRegistration.email are plain str fields with no length upper bound, enabling oversized registration payloads.

subject-reference.title: V5.1.1 — All string inputs have defined maximum length constraints

remediation-tasks.title: Add max_length constraints to UserRegistration fields in schemas.py
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/schemas.py lines 71–72. Ensure `Field` is imported from pydantic. Change `name: str` to `name: str = Field(..., max_length=200)` and `email: str` to `email: str = Field(..., max_length=254)` (254 is the RFC 5321 maximum email address length). These two changes are sufficient; Pydantic returns HTTP 422 automatically on violation.

poam-items.title: Three proxy endpoints accept raw dict bodies — no schema validation performed
poam-items.description: ASVS V5.1.1: /internal/bookings/from-hold, POST /quotes, and POST /quotes/{id}/holds accept dict as their request body type, bypassing all Pydantic validation, length constraints, and type checking.

subject-reference.title: V5.1.1 — All string inputs have defined maximum length constraints

remediation-tasks.title: Replace dict body types with typed Pydantic models for proxy endpoints
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 222, 243, 274 and booking_system_backend/schemas.py. In schemas.py, add three new Pydantic models: (1) `HoldBookingRequest` with fields `hold_id: str = Field(..., max_length=36)`, `user_id: int`, `traveler_name: str = Field(..., max_length=200)`, `traveler_email: str = Field(..., max_length=254)`; (2) `CreateQuoteRequest` with fields `flight_id: int`, `seat_class: str = Field(..., pattern='^(economy|business|galaxium)$')`, `quantity: int = Field(..., ge=1, le=9)`, `user_id: int`; (3) `CreateHoldRequest` with field `user_id: int`. In server.py, import these models and replace `body: dict` with `body: HoldBookingRequest`, `body: CreateQuoteRequest`, and `body: CreateHoldRequest` in the respective route signatures. Access body fields as attributes (`body.hold_id`) rather than dict keys (`body['hold_id']`) when forwarding to the Java service.

poam-items.title: Java CreateQuoteRequest lacks seatClass allowlist and quantity upper bound
poam-items.description: ASVS V5.1.1: seatClass has no @Pattern constraint to restrict it to valid values, and quantity has @Min(1) but no @Max, allowing arbitrarily large seat quantities that could exhaust inventory or cause downstream arithmetic overflow.

subject-reference.title: V5.1.1 — All string inputs have defined maximum length constraints

remediation-tasks.title: Add @Pattern and @Max to CreateQuoteRequest in Java hold service
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_inventory_hold_service/src/main/java/com/galaxium/holdservice/api/dto/CreateQuoteRequest.java lines 21 and 24. Add `import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;` and `import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;` to the import block. On the `seatClass` field (line 21) add `@Pattern(regexp = "^(economy|business|galaxium)$", message = "seatClass must be economy, business, or galaxium")`. On the `quantity` field (line 24) add `@Max(value = 9, message = "quantity must not exceed 9")`. Verify that `@Validated` or `@Valid` is already present on the controller method parameter in QuoteController.java; if not, add `@Valid` to the `@RequestBody CreateQuoteRequest request` parameter.

poam-items.title: GET /user accepts PII (name, email) as URL query parameters
poam-items.description: ASVS V13.1.3: The user-lookup endpoint accepts name and email as URL query parameters, which are logged by web servers, stored in browser history, and may leak to third parties via Referer headers.

subject-reference.title: V13.1.3 — API endpoints do not accept credentials or PII in URL query parameters

remediation-tasks.title: Change GET /user to POST /user with a Pydantic request body
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 202–213. Replace `@app.get('/user')` with `@app.post('/user')`. Change the function signature from `async def get_user(name: str, email: str)` to `async def get_user(body: UserLookupRequest)` where `UserLookupRequest` is a new Pydantic model in schemas.py with fields `name: str = Field(..., max_length=200)` and `email: str = Field(..., max_length=254)`. Update the call to the service function to pass `body.name` and `body.email`. In booking_system_frontend/src/services/api.ts, update the corresponding call from a GET with query params to a POST with a JSON body. Any MCP tool that wraps this endpoint should also be updated to use POST.

poam-items.title: FastApiMCP exposes all unauthenticated routes to AI-agent callers without an auth boundary
poam-items.description: ASVS V13.1.3: FastApiMCP(app) mounts MCP tool bindings for every FastAPI route including all unauthenticated booking, cancellation, and user-lookup routes, expanding the unauthenticated attack surface to AI-agent callers.

subject-reference.title: V13.1.3 — API endpoints do not accept credentials or PII in URL query parameters

remediation-tasks.title: Restrict MCP tool exposure to authenticated routes only
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 336–337. Once the global authentication dependency (POA&M item f1a00002) is in place, ensure `FastApiMCP(app)` inherits it. If the `fastapi-mcp` library supports an `auth_middleware` constructor parameter, pass the `verify_token` dependency there. If not, use the `include_operations` or `exclude_operations` parameter to explicitly allowlist only the MCP tools that should be agent-accessible (e.g. flight search), and exclude booking-mutation and user-lookup tools from the MCP surface until auth is fully enforced.

poam-items.title: No security response headers — application is vulnerable to clickjacking and MIME sniffing
poam-items.description: ASVS V14.4.1: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or Strict-Transport-Security headers are set on any HTTP response, leaving the application exposed to clickjacking and cross-site scripting amplification.

subject-reference.title: V14.4.1 — HTTP responses include appropriate security headers

remediation-tasks.title: Add security response headers middleware to server.py
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py after line 61 (after the CORSMiddleware block). Add a custom Starlette middleware class `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` in the same file or a new `booking_system_backend/middleware.py`. The middleware's `dispatch` method should call `await call_next(request)` and then set the following headers on the response: `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = 'DENY'`, `response.headers['X-Content-Type-Options'] = 'nosniff'`, `response.headers['Content-Security-Policy'] = "default-src 'self'"`, `response.headers['Strict-Transport-Security'] = 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'`. Register it with `app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)` immediately after the CORS middleware block. No external package is required; `from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware` is already available via FastAPI.

poam-items.title: CORS wildcard origin with allow_credentials=True — all origins permitted
poam-items.description: ASVS V14.5.3: CORS_ORIGINS defaults to '*' when unset and CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True, signalling intent to allow credentialed requests from any origin.

subject-reference.title: V14.5.3 — CORS origin validated against explicit allowlist; wildcard not permitted

remediation-tasks.title: Replace CORS wildcard with an explicit origin allowlist
remediation-tasks.description: File: booking_system_backend/server.py lines 53 and 55–61. Change line 53 from `CORS_ORIGINS = os.getenv('CORS_ORIGINS', '*')` to `CORS_ORIGINS = os.getenv('CORS_ORIGINS', '')`. Change the `allow_origins` argument on line 57 from `allow_origins=[CORS_ORIGINS]` to `allow_origins=[o.strip() for o in CORS_ORIGINS.split(',') if o.strip()]` so that the middleware receives a list of explicit origins. Set the `CORS_ORIGINS` environment variable in all deployment configurations (docker-compose.yml, scripts/aws/deploy-to-aws.sh, scripts/ibm/deploy-to-ibm.sh) to the actual frontend origin (e.g. `https://galaxium.example.com`). Keep `allow_credentials=True` only if the frontend genuinely sends credentials; otherwise set it to `False`.

risks.title: Horizontal privilege escalation via unenforced user-ID ownership on booking lookup
risks.description: Any unauthenticated network-reachable caller can enumerate all bookings for any user by iterating integer user IDs.

risks.title: Complete lack of authentication allows unrestricted access to all API endpoints
risks.description: The entire FastAPI application is accessible without any credentials, violating deny-by-default and exposing all booking and user data.

risks.title: Any authenticated user can cancel another user's booking by guessing a booking ID
risks.description: The cancellation endpoint does not compare the booking owner against the caller, enabling unsanctioned data modification.

risks.title: Publicly reachable internal endpoint allows attackers to forge arbitrary bookings
risks.description: The from-hold booking creation endpoint carries no authentication, allowing any attacker to insert arbitrary booking records.

risks.title: Unauthenticated hold operations enable hold hijacking across all users
risks.description: Any caller who knows or can guess a hold UUID can confirm or release another user's hold in the Java service.

risks.title: Unbounded booking name field can be exploited for denial-of-service via oversized payloads
risks.description: Absence of a max_length constraint on BookingRequest.name allows attackers to send arbitrarily large payloads.

risks.title: Unbounded registration fields enable oversized payload attacks on the user registration endpoint
risks.description: No length limit on name and email fields in UserRegistration allows memory exhaustion via crafted registration requests.

risks.title: Unvalidated dict bodies on proxy endpoints accept malformed or malicious JSON without rejection
risks.description: Three proxy endpoints bypass Pydantic validation, allowing type confusion, missing fields, and oversized values to reach the Java service.

risks.title: Unconstrained seatClass and quantity values in Java DTO allow invalid and abusive inputs
risks.description: Missing allowlist and upper bound permit invalid seat classes and arbitrarily large quantities that could corrupt pricing or exhaust seat inventory.

risks.title: PII in URL query parameters is recorded in server logs and browser history
risks.description: User name and email passed as query parameters are captured in access logs and browser history, risking unintended data exposure.

risks.title: MCP tool surface exposes all unauthenticated routes to AI agent callers
risks.description: The MCP mount has no authentication boundary, meaning AI agents can invoke booking-mutation and user-lookup tools without credentials.

risks.title: Missing security response headers expose the application to clickjacking and MIME-sniffing attacks
risks.description: Absence of X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, and HSTS allows browser-based attacks against end users.

risks.title: Wildcard CORS origin with credentials signals acceptance of cross-origin requests from any domain
risks.description: The permissive CORS configuration allows any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the API, enabling CSRF-style attacks.
